The project

Applying for jobs scatters the important facts across tabs, PDFs, forms, and notes. I built Career Agent as an open-source workspace that keeps those pieces on the candidate’s own computer.

The dashboard is the record system: it stores a verified profile, preferences, original documents, sourced opportunities, review packets, and outcomes. Its shared workflow, The Goat, gives Codex or Claude Code the instructions to research jobs and handle browser forms. The candidate chooses whether to submit personally, approve an exact batch, or authorize automatic submission after a separate risk acknowledgment.

My role
Creator of the app and shared agent workflow
Format
MIT-licensed, single-user local application
Storage
SQLite by default; optional Supabase

A search that follows the candidate

Find relevant work

The dashboard reads configured public Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby feeds; the assistant can research more broadly. Career stage, location, compensation, and sponsorship evidence shape which roles deserve attention.

Prepare from real facts

Start here collects the candidate’s background and preferences. Reusable answers, missing questions, portfolio links, and original PDFs flow into versioned packets. Unanswered personal questions stay in the dashboard’s Needs answers queue.

Finish on chosen terms

Form filling and the final Submit click are separate choices. The Goat can hand over a form, submit an exact approved batch, or submit complete applications in automatic mode after the candidate accepts its warning and requests it.

Three ways to finish

You clickSubmit yourself

The assistant can fill supported forms; you review and make the final click.

Exact approvalApprove a batch

Approve specific answers and documents. Any packet change requires fresh approval.

The Goat clicksAsk The Goat to apply

After a separate risk acknowledgment, it may submit complete current forms and record confirmation evidence.

How it works

A typed domain engine sits between the dashboard, storage, and agent tools. It owns application state and approval rules; the user’s assistant handles research and live employer forms.

  1. Dashboard and API

    React shows onboarding, opportunities, Needs answers, review packets, and application history. A local Express API validates requests.

  2. Domain engine

    Shared TypeScript contracts keep eligibility, evidence, packet versions, duplicates, and submission attempts consistent.

  3. Storage and workflow

    SQLite transactions or Supabase revisions persist state. A bounded CLI gives Codex and Claude Code current work without exposing the whole database in every step.

Original PDFs are kept byte-for-byte and checked with SHA-256. The public repository and demo use fictional application data.

A key decision

Permission is specific. Evidence is durable.

Review mode binds approval to the exact job, answers, and documents. Editing a packet invalidates its prior approval. Automatic mode has a separate warning and only runs after the candidate chooses it and asks the assistant to apply.

A ready local packet is never treated as a completed employer form. A click is never treated as a confirmed submission. The record keeps failures, handoffs, and unknown outcomes distinct so a retry does not silently duplicate an application.
